identity.title: POCUS cardiac: qualitative LV systolic function (normal / reduced / severely reduced; EPSS as adjunct) in PLAX/A4C

technique.how: Phased-array probe; obtain parasternal long-axis, short-axis, apical 4-chamber, and subcostal views. Grade LV function visually by endocardial excursion and wall thickening as normal, reduced, or severely reduced. Adjunct: in PLAX M-mode through the anterior mitral leaflet tip, measure E-point septal separation (EPSS); >7 mm suggests reduced EF, >10 mm markedly reduced.
technique.prerequisites: Adequate window in at least one view; awareness of regional wall-motion abnormalities, mitral stenosis, or aortic regurgitation that invalidate EPSS.

interpretation.positive_finding: Visually 'reduced' LV function by trained emergency physicians agrees with cardiology categorization (weighted kappa 0.61, 84-86% agreement) and identifies severe dysfunction with sensitivity 85-93%; EPSS >7 mm was 100% sensitive for LVEF <=30%.
interpretation.negative_finding: A visually normal, vigorously contracting LV makes cardiogenic shock and systolic heart failure unlikely (sensitivity ~100% for LVEF <50% in a decompensated-HF cohort) but does not exclude diastolic dysfunction, valvular disease, or ACS without wall-motion analysis.
interpretation.pitfalls: Tachycardia, hypovolemia, and sepsis cause hyperdynamic function that masks underlying cardiomyopathy; EPSS is unreliable with mitral stenosis, aortic regurgitation, septal hypertrophy, or regional infarcts (sensitivity for severe dysfunction as low as 11-18% in one real-world study). Agreement is poorest in the moderately reduced category (48%).
interpretation.changes_what: Severely reduced: treat as cardiogenic/mixed shock (inotropes, avoid large fluid boluses, cardiology); normal function in hypotension shifts toward distributive/hypovolemic/obstructive causes.

estimates.target_condition: LV systolic function category (normal/depressed/severely depressed) by emergency physician vs blinded cardiologist (agreement, not sensitivity/specificity)
estimates.population: Convenience sample of 51 adult ED patients with symptomatic hypotension (trauma, CPR, and STEMI excluded); 4 EPs with focused echo training
estimates.reference_standard: Blinded cardiologist review of the same 5-view EP echocardiogram
estimates.quote: the weighted agreement between EPs and the primary cardiologist was 84%, with a weighted kappa of 0.61 (p < 0.001)

estimates.target_condition: Severe LV systolic dysfunction (LVEF <=30%) (finding: EPSS >7 mm measured by ED ultrasound fellows)
estimates.population: Sequential convenience sample of ED patients undergoing comprehensive transthoracic echocardiography (n reported in full text)
estimates.reference_standard: Calculated LVEF on comprehensive cardiology TTE
estimates.quote: EPSS measurement of greater than 7 mm for severe systolic dysfunction (LVEF<=30%) were 100.0% (95% confidence interval, 62.9-100.0) and 51.6% (95% confidence interval, 38.6-64.5)

estimates.target_condition: LVEF <50% on comprehensive echo (finding: EP visually estimated reduced LVEF)
estimates.population: 61 ED patients with possible decompensated heart failure receiving FOCUS; 24 (39%) had LVEF <50%
estimates.quote: higher specificity than estimated LVEF (100% sensitivity [95% CI 86-100], 59% specificity [95% CI 42-75])

estimates.target_condition: LVEF <50% on comprehensive echo (finding: EPSS >10 mm measured by emergency physician)
estimates.population: 61 ED patients with possible decompensated heart failure receiving FOCUS; 24 (39%) had LVEF <50%
estimates.quote: MAPSE demonstrated lower sensitivity than EPSS (79% sensitivity [95% CI 58-93], and 76% specificity [95% CI 59-88])

estimates.target_condition: Severe LV dysfunction on cardiology TTE (finding: visual estimation by blinded ultrasound-fellowship-trained EP, reader 1; reader 2 sensitivity 93%)
estimates.population: 113 adult ED patients with both EP point-of-care echo and comprehensive cardiology TTE (Simpson's method)
estimates.reference_standard: Simpson's biplane LVEF on comprehensive cardiology-performed TTE
estimates.quote: Sensitivity of severe dysfunction was moderate to high in VE (EP1 85% and EP2 93%)

sources.citation: Moore CL, Rose GA, Tayal VS, Sullivan DM, Arrowood JA, Kline JA. Determination of left ventricular function by emergency physician echocardiography of hypotensive patients. Acad Emerg Med. 2002;9(3):186-193.

Randazzo MR, Snoey ER, Levitt MA, Binder K. Accuracy of emergency physician assessment of left ventricular ejection fraction and central venous pressure using echocardiography. Acad Emerg Med. 2003;10(9):973-977.

McKaigney CJ, Krantz MJ, La Rocque CL, Hurst ND, Buchanan MS, Kendall JL. E-point septal separation: a bedside tool for emergency physician assessment of left ventricular ejection fraction. Am J Emerg Med. 2014;32(6):493-497.

Bahl A, Johnson S, Altwail M, et al. Left ventricular ejection fraction assessment by emergency physician-performed bedside echocardiography: a prospective comparative evaluation of multiple modalities. J Emerg Med. 2022;62(3):335-341.
Schick AL, Kaine JC, Al-Sadhan NA, et al. Focused cardiac ultrasound with mitral annular plane systolic excursion (MAPSE) detection of left ventricular dysfunction. Am J Emerg Med. 2023;68:52-58.

safety_scope.do_not_use_when: Do not use qualitative LV assessment to exclude ACS (regional wall motion requires more views and expertise) or to grade function precisely for medication decisions; do not rely on EPSS with mitral/aortic valve disease or septal hypertrophy.
safety_scope.escalation_warning: Severely reduced LV function with hypotension or pulmonary edema is cardiogenic shock until proven otherwise: early cardiology/ICU involvement and avoid empiric large-volume fluids.
safety_scope.interobserver_note: EP-cardiologist weighted kappa 0.61 (Moore 2002) and kappa 0.58 for visual global function (McKaigney 2014); agreement is high for normal (92%) and poor for moderately reduced (48%) categories (Randazzo 2003). Two fellowship-trained EPs had kappa 0.94-0.97 vs gold standard for visual estimation (Bahl 2022).
safety_scope.skill_assumption: Emergency physician or hospitalist with focused cardiac ultrasound training (published cohorts: credentialed EP sonographers after 3-hour to fellowship-level training); accuracy assumes at least one adequate window and visual grading into three categories rather than a numeric EF.

extraction_notes: The anchor (Moore 2002) reports agreement (r 0.86, weighted kappa 0.61), not sensitivity/specificity; it is entered as an estimate with null accuracy fields so the quote and location are preserved. Randazzo 2003 similarly reports agreement (86.1% overall) and is cited without a numeric estimate. Sensitivity/specificity estimates come from three single-centre ED studies with different thresholds (EPSS >7 mm for LVEF <=30%, McKaigney; EPSS >10 mm and visual estimate for LVEF <50%, Schick; visual estimate for severe dysfunction, Bahl) and are kept as separate entries. Bahl 2022 reports per-reader sensitivities only (85%/93%); specificity was not in the abstract. No pooled meta-analysis of EP qualitative LV assessment was found in PubMed searches. All locations are abstracts (none of these journals in PMC).
